attempts.summary: Discovered the real physical topology (node3-lan-a-node1-transit-node2-lan-b-node4, a two-hop chain), started a persistent HTTP service on node4:8080, published it via a port-forward (DNAT) on node2's transit address (10.10.12.2:80), and wired up all routing (node1 forwarding lan-a to transit, node3's route to the transit subnet via node1, node2's return route to lan-a via node1, and node4's return routes to transit/lan-a via node2) so node3 reaches the service by asking node2 rather than addressing node4 directly. Verified node3 cannot reach node4 directly. All 4 nodes were restarted one at a time (node4, node3, node1 VyOS, node2 OPNsense) with confirmed boot-identity changes and full post-restart recovery of addressing, routes, NAT/firewall rules, and the working service path.
